meta.author: bobcatfish
meta.body:
i think the rest of this doc does a great job of not trying to specify a solution - but these last 3 requirements seem to assume we're going with feature flags. maybe we can reword them as something like:

1. The maturity of each feature should be clearly documented and it should be clear how to opt into optional features
2. Tools should be available to test all desired combinations of features at various maturity levels
3. It should be possible for a Tekton operator to restrict access to alpha features

I'm not 100% sure about (3): if we go with feature flags this is possible, but i dont totally understand if we actually _need_ it - do we want to be able to say that Tekton operators can restrict access to all alpha features, e.g. even alpha CRDS? (if yes then (3) makes sense to me)

meta.author: afrittoli
meta.body:
After reading and re-reading this a few times, I'm starting to lean towards using a different flag (the name is not good, sorry):
```
data:
 extra-api-fields: ["current" | "alpha" | "beta" ]
```

Where "current" means only the API fields that are on by default in the current API, "beta" means enable "beta" fields only in the current API, "alpha" means enabled "alpha" and "beta" fields in the current API.

What I'm trying to avoid is the case of someone enabling "alpha" fields and disabling "beta" ones. 
If a user / operator wants to stay to up date with the latest and greatest features from Tekton, then they will enable "alpha" level features. If they want to have a single feature that is in alpha and do not want anything else, then this solution won't work for them anyways, because it does not allow to pick specific features. 

Another aspect that needs to be clarified is whether the version that we serve are all immutable except for the last. Once we have `v1`, will `v1alpha` and `v1beta` be frozen and eventually removed? Will new fields only ever be added to `v1` as `alpha` fields first?

meta.author: afrittoli
meta.body:
I think we need to define what the lifecycle of such a feature flag would look, something along the lines of:
- introduce a feature flag, default to current behaviour
  - promote the new feature as experimental in the release notes
  - maintain a table of experimental features and their flags 
- after X time, change the flag to default to the new behaviour, deprecate the existing behaviour
  - highlight the change in the release notes
  - document the flag as a fix for the common symptoms of the change of default in the FAQ on github discussions
  - maintain a table of deprecated features
  - log ~spammy warnings when the feature flag enables a deprecated feature
- after X time, remove the flag and support for the old behaviour from the code

meta.author: unknown
meta.body:
Echoing @afrittoli 's comment above - I don't think users should be able to enable alpha fields while disabling beta ones because it seems reasonable to me for alpha fields to augment functionality introduced in beta fields. Disabling beta while enabling alpha would make that potentially quite hairy?  Suggested change:

```
If the underlying CRD has a version of v1, the webhook admission controller
will be updated to support the feature under the `enable-beta-api-fields` flag
in addition to its existing support under the `enable-alpha-api-fields` flag.
```

meta.author: pritidesai
meta.body:
Here, `alpha` and `beta` are referring to individual features and not overall type version which is represented using `APIVersion`.

The highest `APIVersion` we have is `v1beta1`. When I am introducing a new feature in `v1beta1`, it will considered as `alpha` level support. After many iterations and improvements, we can upgrade that feature to `beta` in the same API `v1beta1` but not to `GA`.

A year from now, our highest `APIVersion` would be `v1` (may be). I am guessing this proposal allows us to introduce an `alpha` feature in `v1`. In that case, irrespective of what `APIVersion` we are on, we will need to serve all lower possible levels, i.e. for `v1` types, we will need `alpha` and `beta` flags.

meta.author: vdemeester
meta.body:
> Are fields always added to the latest available API version?

Yes

> How do make sure APIs are "round-trippable" ?

As we do now, but that's one reason to be able to add field to the latest available API version, so that we don't need to think about round-trippable APIs when `v1alpha1` and `v1beta1` are gone

> How does an API field move from alpha to beta to v1 exactly?

I am not fully sure I understand the question 🤔 

> Can a deployment have alpha flags enabled and beta flags disabled?

I think we shouldn't, as you commented above.

meta.author: vdemeester
meta.body: We should assume we have `v1` and only that version here. But yes, except if you look at documentation, looking at a random yaml, you might not know if the field is alpha, beta or ga.

meta.body:
That's way better @afrittoli ! Thank you!

How about this naming:

`enable-api-fields: ["stable" | "alpha" | "beta" ]`

"Stable" still isn't perfect but I think it's okay? Another option would be to initially add only:

`enable-api-fields: [ "alpha" | "beta" ]` with `beta` being the default (i.e. the greatest stability level we support), and when we move to v1 we'd update it to be `enable-api-fields: [ "v1" | "alpha" | "beta" ]` with v1 as the default?
